words: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Fātiḥa, ṣirāṭ is the object, al-mustaqīm its adjective, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim apposes the preceding phrase, and the remaining clauses modify or coordinate with it.
rows.anchor: مفعول ، و ' المستقيم ' صفة للصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Syntactic relations are not lexical meanings: word order is not itself a word, and inflection cannot be two signs with one serving as the other's explanation.
rows.anchor: ترتيب اللفظ لا يكون لفظا ، والإعراب وإن كان يكون لفظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Individual words were established to be joined so that benefits arise between them, not simply to disclose their meanings in isolation.
rows.anchor: الألفاظ المفردة التي هي أوضاع اللغة لم توضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Language conventions presuppose something already known: a name or pointing gesture identifies a known thing among others rather than creating knowledge of its referent.
rows.anchor: فمحال أن يوضع اسم أو غير اسم لغير معلوم ، ولأن المواضعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposition becomes intelligible through a composed sentence, either verb with noun or noun with noun; the relation of an event to its subject is not itself a lexical meaning.
rows.anchor: لا يعقل إلا من مجموع جملة فعل واسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge to name “these” assumes the angels can already identify the beings indicated, illustrating that names point to known referents.
rows.anchor: وهم لا يعرفون المشار إليهم بهؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun alladhī lets a clause describe a definite noun, just as dhū lets a generic noun describe another noun.
rows.anchor: اجتلب ليكون وصلة إلى وصف المعارف

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: A reported account says clauses are indefinite because they convey new information, so they can modify indefinites but not definites.
rows.anchor: أن الجمل نكرات كلها بدلالة أنها تستفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjānī refines that account: alladhī introduces a clause already known as a story, distinguishing a particular person from others for the hearer.
rows.anchor: إنه إنما اجتلب حتى إذا كان قد عرف رجل بقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when the relative clause gives new information about the person, its event must already be known in general; the hearer learns which person it describes.
rows.anchor: لمن لم يعلم أن رسولا قدم

words: وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people asserted and believed that the angels possessed female attributes; calling them daughters followed from that belief, rather than being a bare naming act.
rows.anchor: أنهم أثبتوا للملائكة صفة الإناث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's question about whether they witnessed the angels' creation shows that the claim concerned an asserted attribute; mere labeling would merit little blame and would not amount to unbelief.
rows.anchor: لم يعتقدوا إثبات صفة ومعنى بإجرائه عليهم

words: قل لئن اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يأتوا بمثل هذا القرآن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is a grave error for believers in the Qur'an's inimitability to turn away from the proof of that inimitability and follow another path.
rows.anchor: ويؤمنون به ويدينون بأن القرآن معجز ثم يصدون بأوجههم عن برهان الإعجاز

words: وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjānī rejects reading jaʿala here as mere naming: the speakers asserted that the angels were female and believed the attribute existed in them.
rows.anchor: ولكن على الحقيقة التي وصفتها لك

words: وجعلوا الملائكة الذين هم عباد الرحمن إناثا
rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj gives the preferred gloss: jaʿala means to say something of an object and judge it to have a quality, as in calling Zayd the most learned.
rows.anchor: الجعل هاهنا في معنى القول والحكم على الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Metaphor is not a transfer of a word's name but a claim to its meaning: calling a man a lion implies courage, understood by inference as in metonymy.
rows.anchor: الاستعارة كالكناية في أنك تعرف المعنى فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic challenge must name a quality the challenged audience can recognize; otherwise neither a valid demand nor proof of incapacity exists.
rows.anchor: مطالبة بأن يأتوا بكلام على وصف ولا تصح المطالبة بالإتيان به على وصف من غير أن يكون ذلك الوصف معلوما للمطالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ring analogy shows that inability cannot be established until the claimed craft is shown and the other person tries to produce that known thing.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يصح وصف الإنسان بأنه قد عجز عن شيء حتى يريد ذلك الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an's distinguishing quality cannot lie in individual words or their ordinary lexical meanings, since these existed before its revelation.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون في الكلم المفردة لأن تقدير كونه فيها يؤدي إلى المحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is not merely to reproduce Qur'anic sound sequences or meter; that reduction would make the challenge as absurd as Musaylima's imitations.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون هذا الوصف في تركيب الحركات والسكنات حتى كأنهم تحدوا إلى أن يأتوا بكلام تكون كلماته على تواليها في زنة كلمات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “they deceive God / God deceives them” and “they schemed / God schemed,” both clauses are God's report, unlike quoted speech followed by God's separate assertion.
rows.anchor: لأن الأول من الكلامين فيهما كالثاني في أنه خبر من الله تعالى

words: قالوا أنؤمن كما آمن السفهاء ألا إنهم هم السفهاء
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that they are fools is detached from the hypocrites' quoted question, since conjunction would make them call themselves fools; a declarative sentence also does not coordinate with a question.
rows.anchor: لكان يكون قد أدخل في الحكاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening alā marks God's independent assertion that they are corrupters; attaching it to their quoted claim would make them describe themselves as corrupters.
rows.anchor: مستأنفا مفتتحا بألا لأنه خبر من الله تعالى بأنهم كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a clause may sometimes coordinate directly with qālū, here that would make God's statement part of the conditional answer, because qālū itself answers a condition.
rows.anchor: ها هنا جواب شرط . فلو عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjānī urges readers to compare their former repetition of unexplained expressions with their new ability to understand verbal composition and explain eloquent speakers' aims.
rows.anchor: قصاراك أن تكرر ألفاظا لا تعرف لشيء منها تفسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Announcing a subject through a pronoun and then explaining it is more emphatic than stating the proposition abruptly, because the advance notice acts like a repeated assertion.
rows.anchor: ثم فسر كان ذلك أفخم له من أن يذكر من غير تقدم إضمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This emphatic construction suits denials, suspicion, false claims, and surprising contradictions, as shown by Qur'anic examples where the added clause confirms or exposes what was disputed.
rows.anchor: هذا الضرب من الكلام يجيء فيما سبق فيه إنكار من منكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Studying why expression is eloquent has religious value: it helps prevent errors about revelation and interpretation and equips readers to give a persuasive argument for a Qur'anic verse.
rows.anchor: سببا إلى حسم كثير من الفساد فيما يعود إلى التنزيل
